name: Mata Kuan Rani Temple
deity: Mandarava, the 'Princess of the Well'
significance: A slate-roofed shrine built over a deep well on the bank of the Beas at Mandi, honouring the princess Mandarava. It is venerated by Tibetan Buddhists and Hindus alike, linking the town to the Padmasambhava tradition centred on nearby Rewalsar.
story: Legend says the king condemned Mandarava and Padmasambhava to a seven-day fire, and when the smoke cleared a lake had formed with a lotus at its centre, convincing the king of the master's power.

name: Gurudwara Buddha Johad
place: Dabla, Raisinghnagar tehsil, Sri Ganganagar district
deity: Guru Granth Sahib; the gurdwara commemorates Bhai Sukha Singh and Bhai Mehtab Singh
significance: A Sikh shrine in the Rajasthan desert marking the spot to which Sukha Singh and Mehtab Singh carried the head of Massa Ranghar, the Mughal official who had desecrated the Golden Temple in 1740. It is one of the principal historical gurdwaras of the Sri Ganganagar district.

name: Parshuram Temple, Chiplun
place: Parshuram village, Chiplun taluka, Ratnagiri district
deity: Parashurama, the sixth avatar of Vishnu
significance: Also called Shree Kshetra Parshuram, this Konkan hill temple was raised in 1700 on the initiative of Swami Paramhans Brahmendra, with funding from the Siddi commander Rasul Yakut Khan. It is the principal shrine of Parashurama in the region his myth claims he created.
story: Tradition holds that Parashurama shot an arrow into the Arabian Sea to push it back and reclaim the Konkan, then chose the Mahendragiri peak here as his permanent home.

name: Jurahareswarar Temple
deity: Shiva, worshipped as Jurahareswarar (Jvarahareswara)
significance: A small Pallava-period Shiva shrine in Kanchipuram, attributed to Narasimhavarman II, though some scholars place it instead in the reign of the Chola king Kulottunga III. Its name means 'remover of fever', and the deity is invoked against sickness.
story: The legend holds that Shiva opened his third eye and the fire that issued from it struck the devas with fever, and that they were cured by praying to him and bathing in the waters of this place.

name: Konetirayala Swamy Temple
deity: Venkateswara, worshipped here as Konetirayudu
significance: A Venkateswara temple in the village of Keelapatla near Palamaner, where the deity carries the local name Konetirayudu. It draws pilgrims travelling the Chittoor district route towards Tirumala.
story: Local tradition says Venkateswara set his foot at Keelapatla first, before going on to Tirumala.

name: Sri Peddamma Thalli Temple
deity: Peddamma Thalli, a form of the Divine Mother
significance: A village-goddess shrine in the middle of Jubilee Hills, Hyderabad, dedicated to Peddamma Thalli as a form of the Mother goddess. It is one of the busiest neighbourhood temples in the city, with a large annual Bonalu observance.

name: Arjunesvara Siva Temple
deity: Shiva as Arjunesvara (the article's infobox lists Vishnu)
significance: One of the many small medieval shrines of Bhubaneswar's old town, built of grey sandstone laid as dry masonry in the Kalinga manner. It is dated to the 12th–13th century and survives as part of the city's dense temple landscape.

name: Chakreshvari Siva Temple
deity: Shiva, as a lingam set in a circular yonipitha
significance: A modest rekha-order shrine on Hatiasuni lane in Bhubaneswar's Rajarani Colony, holding a Shiva lingam in a circular yonipitha. It is dated to the 10th–11th century and belongs to the temple cluster around the Rajarani complex.

name: Brahma Temple, Bindusagar
deity: Brahma, with Bhuvaneshvari as consort
significance: A late-Kalingan shrine on the Bindusagar tank in old Bhubaneswar, unusual in India for having Brahma as its presiding deity. It was built under the Gajapati rulers and is tied ritually to the Lingaraja temple nearby.
story: It is said that Brahma came to Lingaraja's coronation and promised to return every year in the month of Chaitra to serve as the charioteer of Lingaraja's car.

name: Aryankuzhi Devi Temple
deity: Aryankuzhi Bhagavathi, a swayambhu panchaloha image of Parvati
significance: A Bhagavathi shrine in southern Kerala whose presiding image is held to be swayambhu, self-manifested rather than installed. It serves as a local Devi centre in the Thiruvananthapuram district.
story: The temple's origin story tells of a child who fell on a rock that then bled; astrologers read a divine presence in the sign, and worship at the spot grew into the temple.

name: Banapuriswarar Temple
deity: Shiva as Banapuriswarar, with the goddess Somakamalambal
significance: A Shiva temple in Kumbakonam whose name and myth tie it to the story of the town's origin as the place where the pot of amrita came to rest. Shiva is worshipped here as Banapuriswarar alongside the goddess Somakamalambal.
story: The legend holds that this was the spot from which Shiva took aim with his bow and arrow at the floating pot of amrita.

name: Bata Mahadeva Temple
deity: Shiva, as a lingam in a circular yoni pitha
significance: A small pidha-deula shrine standing in the middle of a road in old Bhubaneswar, also known as Mukteswara Shiva. Its pancharatha plan places it in the late Kalingan sequence of the 15th–16th century.
story: It is said that Mahadeva rested at this spot when he visited Ekamra Nagari, and because the shrine sits in the middle of the road he is called Bata Mahadeva, the lord of the way.

name: Hanuman Temple, Kedara-Gouri
deity: Hanuman, as a two-armed image
significance: A laterite shrine on the Kedara-Gouri road in Bhubaneswar's old town, housing a two-armed Hanuman. It is one of the later Kalingan-style structures in the historic temple quarter.

name: Chakrapani Temple
deity: Chakrapani (Vishnu as the Sudarshana chakra), with Vijayalakshmi Thayar
significance: One of the principal Vishnu temples of Kumbakonam, where the deity is worshipped in the form of the discus Sudarshana rather than as an anthropomorphic image. Lacking inscriptions, it is dated to the 15th century on the evidence of its granite walls, five-tiered rajagopuram and carved pillars.
story: The legend tells that the Sudarshana chakra humbled the pride of Surya, who then worshipped it until his powers were restored.

name: Byamokesvara Temple
deity: Shiva, as a lingam in a circular yonipitha
significance: Also called the Suresvara Mahadeva temple, this 10th-century shrine stands inside the Tala Bazaar market complex in old Bhubaneswar. Built of coarse grey sandstone in dry masonry, it is locally attributed to the Somavamsi (Kesari) rulers.

name: Bharati Matha Temple
deity: Shiva
significance: A monastic establishment with a Shiva shrine in Bhubaneswar, said to have been founded by Yayati Kesari, the builder of the Lingaraja temple, and to have first housed the artisans working on that project. It is dated to the 11th century and built in the Kalinga manner.

name: Baitala Deula
deity: Chamunda, known locally as Kapalini
significance: An 8th-century shrine in Bhubaneswar built to the barrel-roofed khakara plan, a form reserved in Kalinga for goddess temples. Its tantric Chamunda sanctum and dense iconographic programme make it one of the most studied early temples of Odisha.

name: Andarkoil Swarnapureewarar Temple
deity: Shiva, as Swarnapureewarar
significance: A Shiva temple at Andankoil in the Valangaiman taluk of Tiruvarur district, built in the Dravidian manner. Its founding tradition connects it to a minister of the legendary king Muchukunda.
story: The story goes that the minister Kandadevar found a shivalinga after Shiva appeared to him in a dream and built a temple over it, and that King Muchukunda had him beheaded before realising his error and restoring him to life.

name: Isanesvara Siva Temple
deity: Shiva; the sanctum retains only the circular yonipitha, the lingam being lost
significance: A rekha-deula Shiva shrine in Bhubaneswar assigned on stylistic grounds to the 13th century and the Ganga period. Its lingam has disappeared, leaving the bare yonipitha in the sanctum.

name: Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, Mumbai
deity: Laxminarayan Dev with Ghanshyam Maharaj, and Radha Krishna Dev with Hari Krishna Maharaj
significance: The main Swaminarayan Sampraday temple in Mumbai, in the crowded Bhuleshwar quarter. The first temple was completed in 1868 by Ranchhoddas Pranjeevandas, and the present three-spired shikharbandh structure replaced it in 1903 under Acharya Lakshmiprasadji Maharaj.

name: Madhangeeswarar Temple
deity: Shiva
significance: A small Shiva temple in Kanchipuram, also called Matangesvara, believed to have been built by the Pallavas at the close of the 8th century. It is noted for dvarapalas carved with four arms.

name: Sivatirtha Matha, Old Town
deity: Shiva as Lingaraja
significance: A matha of the Shankaracharya sampradaya at Rathagada Chowk in old Bhubaneswar, its precinct holding pidha-order shrines in the Kalinga manner. It has a formal role in the Lingaraja temple's festival calendar.
story: Tradition holds that Lingaraja himself comes to this matha to take the community meal during Dola Purnima.

name: Mangala Temple, Patia
deity: Mangala, a four-armed form of Durga
significance: A 19th-century pidha-deula goddess temple in Patia village on the northern edge of Bhubaneswar, enshrining a four-armed Mangala. It is the village's principal shrine.

name: Manibhadresvara Siva Temple – I
deity: Shiva, as a lingam in a circular yoni pitha
significance: One of a pair of small Kalingan Shiva shrines of this name in Bhubaneswar, dated on architectural grounds to about the 14th century. Local tradition credits the Somavamsi (Kesari) rulers, an attribution the building's own features do not support.

name: Manibhadresvara Temple – II
deity: Shiva
significance: The second of the two Manibhadresvara shrines in Bhubaneswar, a rekha deula of the Kalingan type. The article's dating is inconsistent, giving both an 8th-century origin and a 12th–13th-century date for the structure.

name: Chintamanisvara Siva Temple
deity: Shiva, as a lingam with a yonipitha
significance: A 14th-century rekha-deula Shiva temple at the end of Chintamaniswar road off the Cuttack–Puri road in Bhubaneswar. Local tradition ascribes it to the Kesari (Somavamsi) kings.

name: Akhadachandi Temple
place: Badu Sahi, Old Town, Bhubaneswar, Khordha district
deity: Mahishasuramardini
significance: A 10th-century goddess shrine on the south-western embankment of the Bindusagar tank in old Bhubaneswar, built of coarse sandstone to the barrel-roofed khakhara plan. It is also known as the Anshuman temple, and the image of Mahishasuramardini faces east while the building faces south.

name: Devi Jagadambi Temple
deity: Parvati, worshipped as Jagadambika
significance: One of the western group of Khajuraho temples, built under the Chandelas around 1000–1025 CE and dedicated to the goddess Jagadambika. Three encircling bands of sculpture make it among the most richly carved shrines on the site.

name: Gosagarsevara Mandapa
deity: Shiva, as Gosagaresvara
significance: A pillared mandapa in the Gosagaresvara precinct of old Bhubaneswar, built in the Kalingan manner. It serves as the public viewing hall during the annual Durgastami procession.
story: It is said that Lingaraja comes to the Gosagaresvara precinct at Durgastami to wash away his sins, and is then shown to the people at this mandapa.

name: Gangesvara Siva Temple
deity: Shiva, as a lingam within a circular yonipitha
significance: A rekha-order Shiva temple in Bhubaneswar raised under Eastern Ganga rule in the 13th–14th century, the standing fabric being a later renovation. Its name links it to the Ganga river goddess.
story: The legend holds that after Parvati defeated the demons, Shiva struck his trident into the ground to raise a spring, and Ganga and Yamuna were called to consecrate it.
